**Revised Narrative**

The differential metabolite profile is enriched for **Leukotriene C4 Synthesis Deficiency** (SMPDB SMP00353, RaMP top-1 pathway, FDR = 0.0, fold-enrichment = 735.3), with arachidonic acid (C00219), leukotriene A4 (C00909), 5-HETE (C04805), 11,12,15-THETA (C14782), 15-HETE (C04742), 15-deoxy-Δ12,14-PGJ2 (C14717), and CDP (C00112) all matching this pathway cluster. The Rofecoxib Action Pathway (SMP00087) and the Salicylate-sodium Action Pathway (SMP00708) also appear in the top results at the same significance, consistent with shared eicosanoid-target chemistry.

**Key driver and upstream relationships.** KEGG graph traversal confirms that arachidonic acid (C00219) connects to **Leukotriene A4** (C00909) and **5-HETE** (C04805) via a two-hop route through the intermediate C05356 (bidirectional to C00909; forward to C04805), placing arachidonic acid upstream of the leukotriene and lipoxygenase branches. The three HETE species (5-HETE, 15-HETE, 11,12,15-THETA) reflect 5-, 12-, and 15-lipoxygenase activity on arachidonic acid.

**Biological significance.** Coordinated differential abundance of leukotriene A4, multiple HETEs, and 15-deoxy-PGJ2 suggests simultaneous engagement of the lipoxygenase and cyclooxygenase arms of the eicosanoid cascade. Such a pattern is characteristic of inflammatory or eicosanoid-directed perturbations. The presence of CDP hints at phospholipid remodeling concurrent with the eicosanoid surge, linking membrane turnover to the observed metabolite cluster.

**Limitations.** The pathway labels used here (Leukotriene C4 Synthesis Deficiency, Rofecoxib Action Pathway, Salicylate-sodium Action Pathway) are drawn directly from the RaMP enrichment output. KEGG map identifiers (map00590, etc.) and SMPDB SMP00075 were not in the tool-returned pathway list and were excluded. Directional upstream/downstream claims reflect KEGG graph reachability and do not imply direction of differential abundance in the original study.
